result.topic_en: Calculations in linear elasticity (Navier/Lamé equations): constructing a displacement solution from φ = x/r (a Kelvin-type point-force solution), computing the stress components N, T and the surface traction integral over a sphere.
result.transcription:
$\varphi = \frac{x}{r}$ $(\lambda+\mu)\frac{\partial\theta}{\partial x} + \mu\Delta^2 u = 0$ $\Delta^2\varphi = 2\frac{\partial\frac1r}{\partial x}$
$u = (\lambda+\mu)\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial x} + u'$, $\Delta^2 u' = 0$, $\theta = -2\mu\frac{\partial\frac1r}{\partial x}$ $\theta = (\lambda+\mu)\Delta^2\varphi$
$= \mu\Delta^2\varphi$
$(\lambda+\mu)\frac{\partial\theta}{\partial x} + \mu\Delta^2 u = 0$
$u = (\lambda+\mu)\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial x} + u'$, $\Delta^2 u' = 0$, $\theta = -\mu\Delta^2\varphi$, $\theta = (\lambda+\mu)\Delta^2\varphi + \theta'$, $\theta' = -(\lambda+2\mu)\Delta^2\varphi$
$\varphi = \frac{x}{r}$, $\Delta^2\varphi = 2\frac{\partial\frac1r}{\partial x}$
$u = (\lambda+\mu)\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial x} - 2(\lambda+2\mu)\frac1r = x\frac{\partial\frac1r}{\partial x}(\lambda+\mu) - (\lambda+3\mu)\frac1r$ $\theta = [-...-] -2\mu\frac{\partial\frac1r}{\partial x}$
$v = (\lambda+\mu)\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial y} = x\frac{\partial\frac1r}{\partial y}(\lambda+\mu)$
$w = (\lambda+\mu)\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial z} = x\frac{\partial\frac1r}{\partial z}(\lambda+\mu)$
$\psi = x\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial x} + y\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial y} + z\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial z} - \varphi$ $= \frac{x}{r} - \frac{x}{r} - \frac{x}{r}$
$[-x-]\frac1\mu N_1 = -2\lambda\frac{\partial\frac1r}{\partial x} + 2(\lambda+\mu)\frac{\partial^2\varphi}{\partial x^2} - 4(\lambda+3\mu)\frac{\partial\frac1r}{\partial x}$ $\frac{T_1}{\mu} = (\lambda+\mu)2\frac{\partial^2\varphi}{\partial y\partial z}$
$\frac1\mu N_2 = -2\lambda\frac{\partial\frac1r}{\partial x} + 2(\lambda+\mu)\frac{\partial^2\varphi}{\partial y^2}$ $\frac{T_2}{\mu} = 2(\lambda+\mu)\frac{\partial^2\varphi}{\partial x\partial z} - 2(\lambda+2\mu)\frac{\partial\frac1r}{\partial z}$
$\frac1\mu N_3 = -2\lambda\frac{\partial\frac1r}{\partial x} + 2(\lambda+\mu)\frac{\partial^2\varphi}{\partial z^2}$ $\frac{T_3}{\mu} = 2(\lambda+\mu)\frac{\partial^2\varphi}{\partial x\partial y} - 2(\lambda+2\mu)\frac{\partial\frac1r}{\partial y}$
$+\lambda x\Delta^2\varphi$
$\frac{r}{\mu}X = 2(\lambda+\mu)\frac{\partial\psi}{\partial x} - 4(\lambda+3\mu)x\frac{\partial\frac1r}{\partial x} + 2(\lambda+2\mu)\frac1r$ $-6(\lambda+\mu)x\frac{\partial\frac1r}{\partial x}[-...-]\frac1r$ $\frac{\partial\psi}{\partial x} = -x\frac{\partial\frac1r}{\partial x} - \frac1r$
$\frac{r}{\mu}Y = 2(\lambda+\mu)\frac{\partial\psi}{\partial y} - 2\lambda y\frac{\partial\frac1r}{\partial x} - 2(\lambda+2\mu)\frac{\partial\frac1r}{\partial y}x$ $-6(\lambda+\mu)x\frac{\partial\frac1r}{\partial y}$
$\frac{r}{\mu}Z = 2(\lambda+\mu)\frac{\partial\psi}{\partial z} - 2\lambda z\frac{\partial\frac1r}{\partial x} - 2(\lambda+2\mu)\frac{\partial\frac1r}{\partial z}x$ $-6(\lambda+\mu)x\frac{\partial\frac1r}{\partial z}$
$\psi = -\frac{x}{r}$ [-$\int rr\,d\Pi\,X = 4\pi\cdot\mu\cdot(3\lambda+5\mu)$-] $\int rr\,d\Pi\,X = 4\pi\cdot\mu\cdot2(\lambda+2\mu)$

$N_1+N_2+N_3 = 3\lambda\theta + 2\mu\theta$
$u = (\lambda+\mu)\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial x} + (\lambda+2\mu)u'$ $\theta' = \Delta^2\varphi$ $\theta = -\mu\Delta^2\varphi$
$\frac1\mu N_1 = [-...-] -\lambda\Delta^2\varphi + 2(\lambda+\mu)\frac{\partial^2\varphi}{\partial x^2} - 2(\lambda+2\mu)\frac{\partial u'}{\partial x}$ $\frac{T_1}{\mu} = 2(\lambda+\mu)\frac{\partial^2\varphi}{\partial y\partial z} - (\lambda+2\mu)\left(\frac{\partial w'}{\partial y} + \frac{\partial v'}{\partial z}\right)$
$\frac1\mu(N_1+N_2+N_3) = -(3\lambda+2\mu)\Delta^2\varphi$

$\int\frac{xx}{rr}d\Pi = \int\sin\rho\,\partial\rho\,\partial\psi\cos\rho^2 = \left(-\frac13\cos\rho^3\right)2\pi = \frac{4\pi}{3}$
